rubric.name: reviewed-vocabulary-growth milestone close
criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.

Does every goal predicate in the plan have evidence in the results that would fail if the predicate were false? Read the phase records 002-phase-VG1.md, 003-phase-VG3.md, 004-phase-VG2.md, 005-phase-VG4.md, 006-phase-VG5.md and the tests they cite before judging.

Do the shipped code paths (src/gnd/model_index.py and src/gnd/universe.py; src/gnd/model/_unattended.py, src/gnd/model/_includes.py, src/gnd/commands/checking.py; src/gnd/evolve/service.py, src/gnd/evolve/_includes.py, src/gnd/evolve/cli_service.py) behave as the results and delta say, in particular for models without the unattended mode or without includes, which must be unchanged?

Do the pages (representation-format.md 'Unattended source' and 'Model includes', provenance-and-modality.md 'Evolve admission (D-12)', evolution-contract.md, unattended-growth.md 'Starting from a reviewed vocabulary') state what the code does, each rule in one home?
Is every open question raised in the milestone's records dispositioned in the results (closed, carried with an owner, or an accepted residual), and is any disposition wrong?
Are the close amendments in plan section 11 each supported by the record that raised them, with the prior wording kept?
Every concern's evidence must cite one of the three named files; name the record, code or test line in the observation.
